title.narrative: Zimbabwe Climate Change Adaptation & Sustainable Energy Project (Zim-CCASE)

description.narrative: The major problem that this project seeks to address is the lack of proactiveness to climate change issues by duty-bearers and communities living along the climate frontier. This problem is exacerbated by a limited understanding of climate change and natural resources management laws and policies, a lack of knowledge of platforms for advocacy, and patriarchal stereotypes among others. Against this background, this project seeks to strengthen the capacity of women, people with disabilities and young people, and other marginalized groups to understand and actively participate in climate change, and natural resources management. The project seeks to strengthen the capacity, promote uptake of climate adaptation enterprises, and sustainable energy, and amplify the voice of marginalized community groups in climate change by linking them to local and regional advocacy platforms. This project aims to stimulate climate action among women and marginalized groups through the generation of policy-relevant evidence on climate change and curating it for use by women and youth to reduce their vulnerabilities to shocks and hazards. The intervention will also use evidence generated by CA and other partners in other projects (e.g. resilience, developmental, and humanitarian interventions) in addition to generating own evidence through undertaking specific targeted research. The project will also integrate research findings into local, provincial, and national policies and strategies in order to help effective implementation and adoption of climate related policies, regulations, and programs that reduce women and marginalized people's vulnerability.
